1) there exists a renormalization group transformation in algebraic quantum theory which can be used to study scaling properties of local observables, 2) the scaling limit is a classical or a quantum theory, 3) there exists a unique scaling limit for every theory and 4) there exists a scaling limit which is a quantum theory and has the same scaling properties as the original theory.

the scaling algebra provides a natural setting for the analysis of the short-distance properties of local quantum fields and that the renormalization-group transformations are canonical transformations of this scaling algebra.

the renormalization of quantum field theory can be understood as an action of a renormalization group on the scaling algebra and that the scaling limit of a local quantum field theory is either a classical or a quantum field theory.
